open_points.subject: R0-54 / R0-50 import sources
open_points.text: The sources are the instances on the VPS and on the test rig; the owner picks one for each import. ... The first successful import into production closes the operation for good.
open_points.question: There are two sources and each import takes one, but the first successful import closes the operation for good. Can the second source ever be imported? Or must one import carry both sources?
options: one import carries both sources together
the operation closes only after the owner declares the migration finished
only one source is ever imported
open_points.default_guess: the operation closes only when the owner declares the migration finished; each source is imported at most once

open_points.subject: import projects with their identity
open_points.text: from the source the owner picks — the VPS or the test rig
open_points.question: How does production Registry obtain the source data? Options include a pull over a channel, an export file the owner uploads, or something else. Through which trust boundary does it arrive, and what happens to the VPS instance after the migration?
options: owner exports a file from the source and uploads it in the owner interface
production pulls from the source over the WireGuard tunnel
the VPS instance is retired after import
the VPS instance stays as a test instance
open_points.default_guess: owner-uploaded export file; the VPS instance is retired after a successful import

open_points.subject: create a project / correct a project
open_points.text: a customer reference that is unknown or erased refused (R0-16)
open_points.question: R0-51 says a restricted customer cannot be newly named, and R0-57 says the same for an ended customer. Neither failure is in the create or correct rows. Are both refused on create, and on a correction that changes the customer?
options: both refused on create and on a correction that sets them
refused on create only
open_points.default_guess: refused on create and on any correction that newly names them

open_points.subject: restrict or lift a restriction on a customer
open_points.text: any operation using its restricted personal data is refused unless the law provides an exception
open_points.question: Contact data already reaches only the owner. Which data does a restriction actually cover? Does it cover the address and characteristics of the restricted customer's project objects? Does `context` still return the address to PresuPro and Client Portal while the restriction holds?
options: restriction covers contact data only; context unchanged
restriction also covers the objects of the customer's projects; context withholds the address
open_points.default_guess: covers the customer's contact data and the address of their objects; context keeps customer_ref and withholds the address

open_points.subject: restrict or lift a restriction on a customer
open_points.question: What happens when the owner restricts a customer who is already restricted, or lifts a restriction that does not exist?
options: idempotent, returned unchanged
refused

open_points.subject: agent-authority refusals
open_points.text: unknown or archived project refused; ... a project the session is not granted refused
open_points.question: R0-47 requires that a project outside the session's set is answered exactly as a nonexistent one. The rows for 'add a room' and 'read the agent projection' list a distinct 'not granted' refusal. Must every agent-authority row give a single not_found refusal?
options: single not_found for both cases
distinct refusals
open_points.default_guess: single not_found answer for both cases on every agent-authority operation

open_points.subject: owner sees sessions and requests
open_points.text: the owner sees it in the owner interface (R0-47)
open_points.question: No action lists the registered agent sessions or the pending access requests for the owner. Which actions carry these views, what do they output, and in what order?
options: add 'list agent sessions' and 'list pending access requests' owner actions
fold them into 'read the session's access'
open_points.default_guess: add owner actions listing sessions with their sets and pending requests

open_points.subject: request access / answer an access request
open_points.text: declining changes nothing; the session reads the outcome in its access
open_points.question: Access holds only granted ids, the active project and a version. How does the agent tell a declined request from one still pending? Does a pending request belong in the access read?
options: access read carries the request state (pending/answered)
agent sees only the set; decline is indistinguishable
open_points.default_guess: access read carries the state of the session's last request: pending, granted or declined

open_points.subject: request access to a project / register an agent session
open_points.text: | request access to a project | Cabinet Kernel for one agent session | ... | — |
open_points.question: What happens when Kernel requests access for an unregistered session? What happens when it registers a session id that is already registered?
options: unknown session refused; re-registration returns the existing session
re-registration refused
open_points.default_guess: request for an unknown session refused; re-registering returns the existing session unchanged

open_points.subject: R0-49 / R0-56 automatic erasure
open_points.text: When that date comes, the need to keep the data is assessed again: the owner records a new ground and date, or the data is erased.
open_points.question: No primary action carries Registry's own erasure when a period or holdback ends. How does the owner learn that a holdback or period is due? If the owner does nothing, is the data erased automatically on the date?
options: Registry erases automatically on the date; the owner interface lists items due soon
erasure waits for the owner's assessment
open_points.default_guess: Registry erases automatically when no new holdback is recorded by the date; the owner interface lists items coming due

open_points.subject: R0-37 audit
open_points.text: Every significant operation leaves an audit entry
open_points.question: Which operations are significant: reads of personal data, agent reads, refusals? If writing the audit entry fails, does the operation fail with it?
options: all writes, all personal-data reads and all agent-authority calls; audit atomic with the operation
writes only
open_points.default_guess: every write, every personal-data read and every agent-authority call, including refusals; the operation fails if its audit entry cannot be written

open_points.subject: Network surface — owner interface
open_points.text: the owner interface, reachable from outside only through the owner's VPN, over HTTPS
open_points.question: The service API is closed to VM Agent, but the owner interface is not. Is the owner interface reachable from VM Agent, or from the home LAN without the VPN?
options: owner interface not reachable from VM Agent
reachable from VM Agent but credential-protected
open_points.default_guess: owner interface not reachable from VM Agent; reachable only from the owner's devices via VPN or the home LAN

open_points.subject: onboard_object
open_points.text: a client of the API like any consumer, designed elsewhere; its staff-credential use ends with R0-30, and its role is taken by the owner interface and Kernel flows
open_points.question: Every request now needs a token (R0-27), and Kernel no longer creates projects (R0-41). Is onboard_object retired? Or does it receive a service token of its own, and if so, which operations may it call?
options: retired
gets its own service token for limited operations
open_points.default_guess: retired; project creation only through the owner interface
